source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Set BMC power policy to always-on.
2. System does AC off and check LAN is workable after AC on.
3. Set BMC policy to always-off and check step 2 without power on system

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. BMC LAN should be workable after AC on, no matter system power on or not.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: this case cycles physical AC power to the system (AC off then AC on) after setting the BMC power-on policy, and checks the BMC LAN works after AC-on whether the system powers on or not. historical_reviews.deepseek: NO preserves true-AC semantics and recognizes post-cycle LAN evidence, but incorrectly assumes AC must be hand-switched and does not define policy readback, all-feed de-energization, BMC cold-start milestones, two distinct host-state expectations or restoration.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY / CHANGED adds useful policy semantics, dedicated-SUT, reconnect timing, safe power and recovery controls, but classifies by one possible physical implementation rather than the Project-approved AC method and hybrid automated evidence.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 820/2291 treats the row as physical-only, omitting addressable AC controllers, policy/state correlation, standby-power behavior and deterministic LAN recovery measurements.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-985 draft was inspected only as history. This review independently rejects FULLY AUTOMATABLE because AC cycling is explicitly service-impacting and requires user confirmation even when a remote controller exists; it also rejects MANUAL ONLY because the source does not require a hand-pulled feed.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 lets Project SPEC choose an approved tool/method while preserving true-AC coverage; ED-36 treats controller/timing inputs as readiness; ED-38 requires approval for power control, forbids automatic retry and keeps DUT verdict engineer-owned.

original_test_intent: Verify that after complete AC loss and restoration the BMC management LAN cold-starts and becomes usable independently of the host's configured AC-recovery state: in an Always-On phase the host powers on, while in an Always-Off phase the host remains off but standby-powered BMC networking still recovers.
original_method: Set and read back each Project-mapped AC recovery policy, remove all AC feeds long enough to prove actual de-energization, restore AC through the approved manual or addressable controller, then measure BMC network recovery and the expected host power state. Restore the original policy after both separate phases; software reboot/DC power commands are not equivalent.
manual_activity: An engineer approves the exact DUT/feed topology and AC method, verifies no active work or firmware/storage operation, controls or supervises manual/PDU feed switching, observes physical PSU/host states and owns emergency recovery. Automation can set/read policy only through an approved interface and capture power/network timelines.
required_inputs: Vendor definition and supported command/UI/API for Always-On and Always-Off AC recovery, exact host behavior, policy persistence/readback and original/final policy

Chassis/serial and complete PSU-to-AC-feed-to-PDU-outlet map, redundancy/bus topology, proof that every standby-power feed is removed and that network observer/switch/controller are not on the cycled outlet
Approved AC controller or manual SOP, outlet identity/interlocks, off dwell/discharge criterion, on ordering, maximum cycle count, stabilization and emergency stop
Static/DHCP BMC MAC/IP/lease plan and independent client timeline for physical link, address acquisition, ping/ARP, IPMI/HTTPS/SSH/SOL as applicable, plus bounded recovery time
Dedicated quiescent SUT, clean host shutdown/data protection, no firmware updates, local console, controller recovery, protected credentials, Script version and explicit approval
safety_requirements: AC loss is service-impacting even if remotely controllable. Do not cycle a production/in-use SUT or proceed without explicit confirmation, clean workload/storage state and verified outlet-to-chassis identity.
Do not substitute OS reboot, BMC reset, `chassis power off/on` or DC-cycle behavior for removal/restoration of all AC feeds.
For redundant PSUs, coordinate all feeds according to the approved sequence and prove standby rails/BMC actually become unavailable; one live feed invalidates true-AC coverage.
Keep the PDU/Rack Manager, network switch and monitoring client outside the cycled power domain. Stop if controller mapping is ambiguous or a neighboring chassis/outlet could be affected.
Capture and read back each policy before its cycle. Always-Off refers to host AC-recovery behavior, not permission for the BMC LAN to remain down after standby power returns.

Use one bounded attempt per phase with no automatic retry. Abort on wrong outlet, arcing/power hardware alarm, incomplete discharge, unexpected host state, boot loop, BMC identity change or LAN not recovered within the approved limit.
Preserve first-failure power/network/SEL logs, restore the original policy and intended host state, verify storage/host/BMC health and leave all feeds in the approved final condition.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, validate the policy commands, feed/outlet/chassis topology, quiescence, true-AC method, timers, independent observer, recovery and restoration without controlling hardware.

After approval, set/read only the approved policy, coordinate with the engineer or authorized controller for one true AC cycle per phase, and record monotonic timestamps for AC loss/restore, BMC disappearance/recovery, services and host power state.
Produce separate Always-On and Always-Off results and explicitly compare BMC LAN recovery independent of the different host states.
Do not select outlets, operate AC/PDU, shut down host, expose credentials, retry, alter policy beyond the approved phases or issue DUT PASS/FAIL autonomously.
engineer_actions: Approve the policy mapping, complete feed/outlet topology, AC method, quiescent window, timers, recovery and original-policy restoration.
Perform/supervise all AC operations and physical host/PSU observations, maintain emergency power recovery and confirm the target only.
Verify final policy, host, storage, BMC, network and feed state and issue per-phase plus overall verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its manual AC concept is one valid implementation and its post-cycle LAN check is relevant, but the source does not mandate hand switching. It omits approved remote-PDU capability, policy readback, true all-feed loss and phase-specific host/BMC expectations.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the Project-approved policy interface and AC method—manual or mapped PDU/Rack Manager—only after approval. Collect protected read-only BMC identity/LAN/service and independent host power evidence; never substitute a BMC power command for AC loss.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Always-On and Always-Off phases, true AC off/on, BMC LAN independence, Script URL and 10/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Baseline and read back original policy; run one mapped Always-On true-AC cycle and measure BMC plus host recovery; restore stable baseline; run one Always-Off true-AC cycle and prove BMC LAN recovers while host remains off; restore original policy/state and audit logs.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact AC recovery policy implementation, multi-PSU/feed topology, BMC standby-power/network path and lab controller.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC/CPLD/PSU, network, PDU/Rack Manager and internal Script versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor AC recovery policy and BMC cold-start timing, rack power map and approved lab AC-cycle SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds explicit all-feed proof, phase state matrix, cold-start milestones, controller neutrality and final restoration without changing true-AC intent.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A remote software power cycle provides no AC-loss coverage; a single policy phase cannot demonstrate BMC LAN independence from whether the host auto-powers on.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Policy map, full power topology/controller, timers, independent network observer, recovery and approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect outlet mapping or cycling during writes can affect other equipment or corrupt the host; BMC cold-start time may exceed simple ping timing.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may choose manual switching, PDU or Rack Manager and project-specific policies/timers. It must document the tool, exact target mapping and equivalent true-AC coverage; no software reboot/DC-cycle override may be reported as full coverage.
expected_evidence: Chassis/serial, BIOS/BMC/policy/Script versions, original policy, complete PSU-feed-outlet map, approved AC method and quiescent authorization
Per phase policy set/readback and expected host state, full pre-cycle BMC MAC/IP/services, host/storage and power/feed status
AC-off/on controller or operator timestamps, proof all standby feeds were absent, off dwell/discharge and independent observer continuity
Per phase BMC link/address/lease and management-service recovery timeline with immutable identity plus actual host off/on state and SEL/network/console evidence
Original policy/final host/feed restoration, clean storage/BMC/network health, first-failure preservation, scope deviations and engineer-owned verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require true AC restoration under two host recovery policies and BMC LAN availability in either resulting host state. The exact tool, policy names and timers are Project inputs, not contradictory semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The two phases, target and acceptance are identifiable. A mapped AC method and safety package make the test executable; absence of a remote controller merely changes the manual boundary, not review completion.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Preserves its true-AC and post-cycle evidence intent but removes the unsupported hand-only restriction and adds the two-policy state/timing/recovery contract.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its strong power safety while changing MANUAL ONLY to package/user confirmation because an approved controller and substantial automated verification are valid.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces physical-only treatment with deterministic all-feed, BMC cold-start and host-policy evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Rejects its FULLY AUTOMATABLE class under the explicit power-cycle confirmation rule while keeping its useful distinction between true AC and software power.

review_improvement: Prevents a one-feed or software cycle from masquerading as AC loss, prevents Always-Off from being misread as BMC-off, and makes BMC LAN recovery measurable separately from host power restoration.
independent_technical_reasoning: The engineering question is whether BMC standby networking recovers after a cold AC event regardless of host auto-power policy. A mapped controller can automate the electrical transition, but AC removal remains destructive/service-impacting and always needs approval; manual switching is only one implementation. Package/user confirmation therefore preserves both capability and safety without reducing coverage.
